title: quercus spicata var. depressa
intro: Quercus spicata var. depressa, commonly known as scrub oak, is a type of shrub or small tree found in the southwestern United States and northern Mexico. This plant has been used in traditional medicine for its various health benefits, including treating fever, rheumatism, and skin conditions due to its anti-inflammatory and antimicrobial properties. The therapeutic actions of Quercus spicata var. depressa include its ability to reduce pain and swelling, as well as its potential to act as an antiseptic and antioxidant. The bioactive constituents of this plant include flavonoids, tannins, and phenolic acids, which are responsible for its medicinal properties.
